true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate downsize method definition overrides the width/height variant

The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: once as `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) and again as `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). In Ruby, the second definition completely replaces the first. Any existing caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` (four positional arguments) will now hit the new signature, where `height` is bound to `opts`; since `height` is an Integer and not a Hash, this raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion into Hash`, or at best silently produces a broken dimensions string. The old width/height variant is dead code that can never run. Either remove it or consolidate into one signature that accepts both.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side max upload size hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings

`validateUploadedFile` previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, respecting the admin-configurable `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`. It is now hardcoded to 10MB for both images and attachments. Consequences: (1) on sites where the attachment limit is lower than 10MB, the client will let users pick oversized attachment files and push the whole upload to the server only to be rejected; (2) on sites where the image limit is higher than 10MB, valid uploads are blocked client-side with a wrong error message; (3) it contradicts this PR's own purpose — large images that the server would now automatically downsize are still refused in the browser. Same issue for the hardcoded 10MB in the 413 handler at line 246, which is also shown to users for oversized attachments where the message was previously image-specific.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsizing loop may exit with image still over the limit, then proceeds anyway

The loop runs at most 5 iterations of an 80% resize, which reduces file size by at most ~67% (0.8^5), and only roughly — file size does not scale linearly with linear dimensions. An image that is more than ~3x the configured `max_image_size_kb` will still exceed the limit when the loop exits, yet the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the oversized file, which will then fail with a generic server error instead of either being downsized further or rejected with a clear message. There is no check or handling after the loop for `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`.

In-place downsize (from == to) can corrupt the uploaded file, and failures are not detected

`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path as both input and output. For animated GIFs this dispatches to `gifsicle ... --output <same file>`, and writing the output over the file being read is not a supported/safe operation and can truncate or corrupt the image. Additionally, `downsize` returns false when the `convert`/`gifsicle` invocation fails, but the return value is ignored here; if the external command fails partway through, the (possibly truncated or emptied) temp file is passed straight to `Upload.create_for`, storing a corrupted image. The loop should downsize to a distinct temp path and abort the upload (or fall back to the original) when `downsize` returns false.

Synchronous CPU-heavy image resizing runs in the request thread with no size cap on remote URL downloads

Two related problems: (1) the API URL-download branch now downloads up to 10MB (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`) instead of the site-configured limit, and the subsequent downsize loop with ImageMagick/ImageOptim runs synchronously inside `create_upload` for `synchronous` API requests — a multi-second CPU-heavy operation blocking a web worker. (2) In the deferred path, the same heavy conversion runs in the Scheduler::Defer thread, but the tempfile was created in the request and is fine, yet the client has already been told `success_json` before the resize happens, so any downsizing failure surfaces only as an opaque MessageBus error. Consider capping the download back to a site setting and validating the downloaded size before attempting the resize.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation calls sub! on possibly-nil host

The `before_validation` block runs `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If a request creates/updates a host without a `host` parameter (params[:embeddable_host][:host] is nil or the key is missing), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a validation error. It should guard with `if self.host.present?` so the format validation can report the error properly.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update/destroy crash with 500 when host id does not exist

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown/stale id, then `save_host(host)` calls `host.host = ...` and `host.destroy` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a 404. Should render not_found when the record is missing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator contents swapped between files

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, while spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The files' contents are exchanged. It happens to work because fabricators are loaded globally, but every future edit (e.g. someone adding a category fabricator to the 'right' file or deleting what looks like a duplicate) will be error-prone; the contents should be in their correctly named files.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host values interpolated directly into INSERT SQL

The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by string interpolation. The embeddable_hosts setting was free-form text, so any line containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will break the migration or inject unintended SQL. Values should be quoted/escaped (e.g. via `quote_value` or ActiveRecord inserts).

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category site setting row is absent

The migration does `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. Site settings are only persisted to the site_settings table once changed from their default, so on most installs (where embed_category was never set) the query returns no rows and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and failing the migration for everyone. Same problem on line 15 for the uncategorized_category_id lookup. Both lookups need nil-safe handling (e.g. use `SiteSetting` defaults or guard against empty results).

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

false_positives.candidate:
Host validation regex too restrictive

The format regex requires a dot and a 2–5 letter TLD (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), so valid hosts like `localhost:3000`, `my_host.example.com` (underscore), hosts with new long TLDs, or trailing dots are rejected. Since this list drives which sites can embed comments, admins on intranet/dev setups will be unable to configure valid hosts and will get only a generic format error.

New hosts saved without a category send null and lose user's choice context

For a newly added host, `categoryId` is initialized to null and the category-chooser starts empty; save sends `category_id: null`, which the server silently converts to the uncategorized category. Combined with `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checking host presence and `TopicEmbed.import` using the host's category for new topics, hosts accidentally created without a category will post embedded topics to Uncategorized with no warning. Also, `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` returns undefined for a null category, leaving `host.category` unset after save until reload.

No index on embeddable_hosts.host despite per-request lookup

`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` on every `/embed/comments` and `/embed/count` request (these are high-traffic, cacheable embed endpoints hit by every page view of embedding sites). There is no index on `host`, so each embed request triggers a full table scan once more than a handful of hosts exist. Add an index (on `lower(host)` for Postgres) in the migration.

No request specs for new admin controllers

Both new controller specs only assert the controller's superclass. There are no tests for create/update/destroy of embeddable hosts (including the nil-host-param crash, blank category fallback to uncategorized, and validation error rendering) or for the embedding show/update endpoints. Given this PR replaces a working site-setting mechanism with new endpoints and a data migration, the behavior is essentially untested.

create_table with force: true and irreversible data migration inside change

`create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` will silently drop an existing embeddable_hosts table (data loss if the migration is ever re-run against a partially migrated database). Additionally, the data copy and the `DELETE FROM site_settings` make the migration effectively irreversible while living in a `change` method, so `rake db:rollback` will fail or destroy the old settings with no way back.

expandable_first_post? no longer requires any embeddable host

The check `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && ...` was reduced to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. A stale TopicEmbed with no matching EmbeddableHost (e.g. after the host was deleted, which nothing prevents) will still be treated as expandable, triggering `TopicEmbed.expanded_for` remote fetches for hosts that are no longer allowed. If the host requirement was intentionally dropped, the migration should also clean up orphaned topic_embeds or the retrieval should be validated against EmbeddableHost.

update action is a no-op

PUT /admin/customize/embedding simply re-serializes the current state and ignores the request body entirely, while the new admin UI's `saveChanges` action calls `embedding.update({})` as if it persisted something. The endpoint silently discards any submitted changes; either implement the update or remove the save control so admins are not misled into thinking embedding settings were saved.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists

TopicsController#unsubscribe does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level`. A TopicUser row is only created when a user has viewed/tracked/posted in a topic, but the email unsubscribe link is sent to users who may have received a notification (e.g. via watch category or a mention) without ever having opened the topic. For those users find_by returns nil and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of muting the topic. The code should use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` which upserts the row.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct AR save bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping

unsubscribe mutates the TopicUser record directly with `tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!` instead of going through TopicUser.change. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are never updated (they should be set to user_changed), and no `notification_level_change` MessageBus message is published to `/topic/:id` for that user, so an open tab will keep showing the stale notification level. All other paths that change notification level in the app use TopicUser.change for these reasons.

List-Unsubscribe header not updated to the per-topic URL

MessageBuilder#header_args still sets the List-Unsubscribe header to `user_preferences_url` even when a topic-specific `unsubscribe_url` was supplied in the same opts. Mail clients that use the List-Unsubscribe one-click header will therefore send users to global preferences instead of the per-topic unsubscribe page, defeating the feature for those clients.

No test that the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the email

The spec was only updated to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` so the existing assertions keep passing; there is no assertion that this URL actually appears in the body or html_part, and no controller or mailer spec for the new TopicsController#unsubscribe action (nil TopicUser case, redirect on slug mismatch, toggle semantics). The core behavior of this PR is untested.

State-changing GET endpoint with no CSRF token or confirmation

The unsubscribe action permanently changes the user's notification level (potentially to muted) as a side effect of a plain GET request, with no CSRF token and no confirmation step. Email scanners, link prefetchers (mail clients, antivirus, some browsers) follow links in emails; if the user's browser session is active or the link is fetched through a prefetching proxy that carries cookies, the topic can be muted without the user ever clicking. The rest of the codebase uses keyed, token-protected unsubscribe endpoints (see `email/unsubscribe/:key`); the per-topic link should either be tokened or the GET should only display a page where the change is made via a POST/XHR.

Toggle to 'regular' contradicts the 'stop receiving notifications' message

When the user's level is tracking or watching, the action sets it to `regular`, not `muted`. But a regular user still receives notifications for direct replies and mentions. The email text ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here') and the client locale ('You will stop receiving notifications for...') promise that notifications stop, yet the user will continue to be emailed on replies. Either the action should always mute, or the copy must say notifications are reduced to direct replies only.

unsubscribe_link locale now requires %{unsubscribe_url} for all callers

The server locale `unsubscribe_link` was changed to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and MessageBuilder renders it whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true (both in html_part and body). Only UserNotifications#send_notification_email passes `unsubscribe_url`. Any other caller (plugins, or future core mailers) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without supplying `unsubscribe_url` will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building the email. Either the locale should tolerate a missing URL or the builder should default unsubscribe_url when absent.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation has write side effects: should_block? saves records during model validation

EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and saves the record. This means every User validation run (including intermediate validations, invalid attempts, or any other code path that calls user.valid?) performs a database write. Consequences: side effects from a read-only operation, writes inside validation callbacks, and skewed match_count statistics from repeated failed signup attempts. The statistic update should be decoupled from the predicate (e.g. done only on actual signup attempts in the controller, or via an atomic UPDATE).

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email lookup is case/format sensitive and easily bypassed

BlockedEmail.should_block?(email) does a plain `where(email: email)` match with no normalization (no downcasing, no stripping). Users can trivially bypass the block by registering with different casing (e.g. 'Bad@SpamClub.com' vs a stored 'bad@spamclub.com') or surrounding whitespace. The User model stores emails without downcasing (only some flows use Email.downcase), so a blocked address will still validate successfully whenever the submitted string isn't byte-identical to the stored one. The lookup and the stored records should be normalized (downcase/strip, ideally at both write time in a before_validation on BlockedEmail and at lookup time).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Blocked-email check only runs when email_changed?, skipping existing users

The `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` guard means the BlockedEmail check is skipped for any record whose email attribute was not changed (e.g. a previously-created user whose email was later added to the block list, or records loaded and re-saved). If the intent is only to gate signups this is fine, but the BlockedEmail feature then provides no protection on any path where an existing/loaded user is validated or saved (e.g. password_reset saves the user with the same email). Confirm the guard matches the intended scope of the blocklist.

match_count increment is a read-modify-write race

should_block? increments match_count in Ruby (`record.match_count += 1`) and saves the full record. Under concurrent signup attempts for the same email, increments can be lost, and full-record saves can also overwrite other columns with stale values. Use an atomic counter update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Weak origin check uses substring match on discourseUrl

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that appears anywhere in the discourseUrl string. An attacker page at e.g. `http://evil.com/https://forum.example.com` or an origin like `http://forum.example.com.attacker.com` (which contains the forum origin as a substring) passes the check, and the handler then writes an attacker-controlled `e.data.height` into the iframe height. The check must compare parsed origins for equality, not substring containment.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped URL interpolated into HTML in imported_from footer `contents << "
#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")} "` interpolates the raw feed item URL into an href attribute and link text with no HTML/attribute escaping. A feed entry whose link contains a single quote or angle brackets (e.g. `x' onclick='...`) injects arbitrary markup into the post body, which — combined with the raw_html cook path — is stored and served unsanitized. The URL must be escaped before being embedded in the HTML string.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
request.referer interpolated raw into inline JavaScript

`parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` interpolates the Referer header into a single-quoted JS string with no JS-string escaping. ERB's HTML escaping does not neutralize single quotes or backslashes inside a <script> block (entities are not decoded there), so a Referer such as `http://embeddable-host/'};alert(1);//` breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary script in the embed frame. Use a fixed targetOrigin (the Discourse base URL) or json_escape/j() the value.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Entire feed re-imported every hour; feed_key/dedup key defined but never used

The `feed_key` method builds a redis key for the feed's last-modified state but is never called anywhere. Every hour the job iterates all feed items and runs TopicEmbed.import for each one, performing SHA1 comparisons and (when content changed) full post revisions for every historical item, forever. Feeds commonly keep hundreds of items, so this grows unboundedly. Use the feed's ETag/Last-Modified (the feed_key) or skip items whose URL was already imported.

Feed polling has no error handling and retry disabled, so failures are silently swallowed

Jobs::PollFeed sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and `poll_feed` calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import` for each item with no rescue. If the feed URL is temporarily down, returns malformed XML, or any item raises (e.g. `i.content` nil causing NoMethodError, or an invalid link), the exception propagates and the job dies without retry or notification; hourly polling then effectively stops working with no visibility. Exceptions should be caught/logged, and the whole job should not abort on a single bad item.

Import crashes if the embedded post was deleted

In the update branch, `post = embed.post` may be nil if the topic's first post was deleted (the topic_embeds row is not cleaned up when posts are destroyed). The subsequent `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!` then raises NoMethodError, which in the poll feed job aborts processing of the entire feed. It should check `embed.post.blank?` and re-create or skip instead.

Job requires irrelevant dependency 'email/sender'

The RetrieveTopic job begins with `require_dependency 'email/sender'` although it has nothing to do with email; this appears to be copy-paste residue and loads unrelated mailer code in every sidekiq worker process running this job. It should require only 'topic_retriever'.

Loading view reloads the iframe forever even when retrieval fails

The loading page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds. If the RetrieveTopic job failed (invalid embeddable host, fetch error, embed_by_username unset so TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns early), no TopicEmbed is ever created, and every visitor of the embedding page triggers an endless reload loop plus a new enqueued job per minute per visitor, generating continuous load on both the embedding site and the Discourse instance. The reload should be limited to a few attempts.

RSS-imported HTML is stored and served with no sanitization (raw_html cook method)

TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], and Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for that method, bypassing Discourse's entire markdown/sanitization pipeline. Any script/iframe/event-handler markup present in the RSS feed content (or in a page fetched by TopicRetriever/import_remote from the embeddable host) is stored as-is in `cooked` and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19, and also on the main forum topic page. A compromised or malicious feed/embeddable site therefore gets stored XSS on the Discourse instance. The imported content must be sanitized (e.g. via Sanitize/Nokogiri whitelist) before storing.

force: true added to an already-released migration will drop existing tables

This PR modifies the previously shipped CreateTopTopics migration to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which drops any existing top_topics table before recreating it. On any deployed database where this migration is re-run (db:migrate:redo, restore-from-schema edge cases, or multi-site setups that replay migrations), all accumulated top_topics data is silently destroyed. `force: true` is only appropriate for development scratch tables, never for migrations against production data (same concern applies to the new create_topic_embeds migration, though that table is new).

import mutates the caller's contents string

`contents << "..."` uses String#<< on the argument passed by the caller, permanently appending the 'Imported from' footer to the caller's string. In the poll feed loop this mutates local variables held by SimpleRSS items; if a caller reuses the string (e.g. logs it or compares it), it sees unexpected modifications. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
-ms-align-items is not a real property

The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. There is no such CSS property; the Microsoft pre-flexbox property is `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on the previous line). This dead declaration just bloats the compiled stylesheet on every use of the mixin and suggests the vendor prefix list was copied without verification. It should be removed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
.valign-helper vertical centering hack breaks inside the new flex container

`.d-header .contents` is now a flex container (`@include flexbox()` + `align-items(center)`), but the legacy `.valign-helper { display: inline-block; height: 100%; vertical-align: middle; }` (lines 21-25) remains. In a flex container `vertical-align` is ignored and `height: 100%` resolves against the container's content-box height, so the helper no longer vertically centers its siblings the way it did in the old inline/float layout. Any markup still relying on valign-helper (e.g. in plugins or older header markup) will render misaligned. The rule should be removed or converted to flex-based centering.

float: right on button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container

.small-action was changed to `@include flexbox()`, but its direct child `button { float: right; }` (line ~306-309) still relies on floating. Floats have no effect on flex items, so the button (e.g. the 'delete' action on small-actions) will no longer be pushed to the right edge; it will sit immediately after the description text. It should be replaced with `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container. The `float: left` on `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc .avatar` similarly no longer does anything.

order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper only works when its parent is the flex header

`.extra-info-wrapper` now uses `@include order(2)` with no accompanying display change, so `order` only has an effect when the element happens to be a direct child of a flex container (the header `.contents`). Everywhere else `.extra-info-wrapper` appears (it is also used outside the header, e.g. above the topic list in category pages) the declaration is inert. If reordering is only intended in the header, it should be scoped as `.d-header & { @include order(2); }` to make the intent explicit; otherwise the non-header usages silently keep their DOM order and any layout change there is unintended.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

A rescue/guard around the SiteSetting read (falling back to :en when unavailable) would make this robust.

Fallback translations are not loaded outside the controller path, causing 'translation missing' in jobs/mailers

The only place the fallback locales' translation files get loaded is ApplicationController#set_locale calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Everywhere else (background jobs, Sidekiq, ActionMailer, rake tasks), I18n.translate only triggers load_locale(config.locale), which loads the primary locale's yml files but not the fallback locales (default site locale or :en). When the Fallbacks backend then tries to look up a missing key in an unloaded fallback locale, the backend has no translations for it and the user gets 'translation missing' text instead of the English fallback. The added comment in Cursor.__init__ says negative offsets are now allowed as a 'performance optimization', but the code is unchanged: Cursor.from_string already accepted any int, and nothing in this file handles negative offsets. The PR adds a new paginator class, a new constructor flag (enable_advanced_features), and modifies the core slicing logic of BasePaginator.get_result used by many endpoints, but includes no tests. The same `cursor` string therefore yields different (or broken) results depending on who sends it, and clients cannot rely on the cursor format being stable across pages if a user's permissions change. There is no serialization/test coverage for this alternate response path.

Hardcoded eviction limit of 1000 conflicts with configurable max_segment_spans=1001

The eviction threshold is hardcoded to 1000 in Lua, while SpansBuffer still exposes `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` as a constructor parameter (now unused after the Python-side span-count check was removed from _load_segment_data). The off-by-one mismatch and the dead configuration parameter mean operators who tune `max_segment_spans` (e.g. via options) will have no effect, and the previously-enforced byte-size-only limit no longer matches the documented behavior. The limit should be passed as an ARGV so it stays configurable, or the stale parameter removed.

Redirect-follow loop limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000

The redirect resolution loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations with no explanation and the explanatory comment removed. For traces whose redirect chains exceed depth 1000, the loop exits without resolving to the final set key; the script then writes `hset(main_redirect_key, span_id, set_span_id)` with a non-final `set_span_id`, permanently corrupting the redirect map and causing the trace's spans to be split across multiple segments (data fragmentation) with no error or metric. If the reduction was intentional (e.g. Lua execution time), the failure mode should at least be detectable, and the redirect_depth metric already returned makes the old limit observable — reducing it silently is a behavioral regression.

Undocumented, untested query-parameter-driven paginator switch on a public endpoint

The endpoint now branches on an undocumented `optimized_pagination=true` request parameter and a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with an `enable_advanced_features` flag. This changes pagination behavior for API consumers (cursor format/semantics, result boundaries) based on a hidden flag, has no test coverage anywhere in the diff, and is not mentioned in API docs. The 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' justification in paginator.py is also misleading: the flag gates behavior, not authorization, and the paginator change itself is the risky part. Either remove this path or add tests and document the parameter.

max_segment_spans parameter is now dead after removing the span-count check in _load_segment_data

_load_segment_data no longer enforces `max_segment_spans` (the check and its `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric were deleted in favor of Lua-side eviction), but the constructor still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans=1001`. This is misleading configuration: changing it has no effect, and the docstring/comment contract ('Segments exceeding a certain size are skipped') is now only true for byte size. Remove the parameter or wire it into the Lua script.

zpopmin eviction silently drops span payloads, including possibly the root span

When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, the script calls `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)`, permanently deleting span payloads from the buffer. The evicted spans (those with the earliest end timestamps — which typically includes the root/segment span, since it starts first) are never flushed to the buffered-spans topic; they are silently lost with no metric or log. The previous behavior (skipping oversized segments with an error log and a `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric) at least made the loss observable. Additionally, evicting the root span while still setting the `span-buf:hrs:` key means the flushed segment will have `has_root_span` set but no span with `is_segment: true`, producing malformed segments downstream.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache key uses Python hash(), which is not stable across processes

The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python's built-in `hash()` for tuples of ints is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project-id set produces different keys in different workers/processes. Consequence: cache entries written by one worker can never be read by another (cache hit rate collapses, defeating the stated performance goal), and worse, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 73) computes the key in whichever process handles the config change, so it will almost never delete the keys other workers are reading — stale eligibility can persist well beyond 60s. Use a deterministic encoding such as a sorted, joined string of project ids.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility is checked against the outer dataset, not the scoped dataset actually queried

In `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` uses the closed-over `dataset` variable, but the query is executed against `scoped_dataset`. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `split_dataset` = `discover` or `metrics_enhanced_performance` while the outer `dataset` may be different, so the decision to substitute `upsampled_count()` is made against the wrong dataset. This can either apply a `sample_weight`-based aggregation to a dataset that has no such column (query error) or skip it for an errors-only split query where it should apply. Pass `scoped_dataset` instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental nested git repository / submodule entry committed

The PR adds a `sentry-repo` file containing 'Subproject commit ...', which indicates a nested git checkout was committed to the repository root. This pollutes the repo and should be removed (and gitignored) before merge.

Comments claim caching/consistency behavior the code does not provide

The comments in `_get_event_stats` say the eligibility check is 'cached' and ensures 'consistent behavior across query execution', and `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` is a pointless alias. The helper's own docstring also claims the allowlist is read 'fresh each time', directly contradicting the 60-second cache in the same function. These misleading comments should be corrected or removed since they describe guarantees (freshness, consistency) the implementation explicitly does not have.

Error-focus check inspects the raw request query, not the effective query

`_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET['query']`, but the actual query executed by `_get_event_stats` can be a rewritten one (e.g. the dashboard split path builds `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"`, and other callers pass scoped queries). A discover query that filters errors via the rewritten query but whose original request query lacks `event.type:error` will silently skip upsampling, while an equivalent query phrased differently gets it. The decision should be derived from the query string actually being executed, not the raw request parameter.

No caller for invalidate_upsampling_cache and no cache-invalidation on option change

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never invoked anywhere in this PR, and nothing hooks it to changes of the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option. Combined with the 60s cache and the broken (hash-based) key, removing a project from the allowlist may not take effect for an unbounded time. Either wire invalidation into the option-update path or drop the cache.

Only exact 'count()' is transformed, producing inconsistent mixed-scaled results

`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites only the literal string `count()` and leaves every other aggregation untouched. A request like `yAxis=count(),count_unique(user),p95(transaction.duration)` on an allowlisted errors query will return an upsampled (scaled) count alongside unsampled-based unique/percentile values in the same response, giving internally inconsistent data (e.g. unique users can exceed total count). Aliased forms such as `count() as total` are also missed. Either transform the other supported aggregations or restrict the rewrite to requests whose entire column list can be upsampled.

Snuba endpoint upsampling tests are order-dependent due to shared cache state

`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` writes its result to the shared cache under a key derived from organization id and project ids. The four tests in `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest` use the same org/projects but different mocked allowlists, and nothing clears the cache between them. `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` caches `True`, so the later `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` / `..._with_no_allowlisted_projects` can read the stale cached value and fail (or pass only due to run order). The tests must flush the cache in setUp, and the new unit tests never exercise `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (including its cache branch) at all.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
fetch_error_details zips error_ids with dict values(), misaligning events when any node is missing

`fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, fetches them via `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` (which returns a dict that omits missing nodes and whose `.values()` ordering is not guaranteed to match the requested key order), then constructs ErrorEvents with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. If any error event node is missing from nodestore, or the returned dict order differs, the wrong `event_id` is paired with the wrong event data, and the `if data is not None` filter can drop the wrong entries. This produces incorrect error titles/messages/timestamps sent to Seer for the replay summary. Iterate over `events` items keyed by node_id (or use `get_multi`'s mapping back to event ids) instead of `zip`.

true_positives.matched_candidate:

false_positives.candidate:
Editing bodies of already-shipped data migrations

Migrations 0917 and 0920 have had their data-conversion logic replaced with a no-op and a comment claiming they "had an error and was never run". These migrations have already shipped in releases, and self-hosted installations (or any environment where they did run, e.g. the 0917 migration before the 0920 revision was cut) have them recorded as applied. Mutating applied migrations creates divergence: environments where 0917 ran and inserted GroupSearchView rows will also run 0921 ("rerevised"), which may duplicate or conflict with rows created by 0917, since 0917 can no longer be inspected for what it did. The corresponding test for 0917 was also deleted. The safe pattern is a new corrective migration, not rewriting history; at minimum this needs a clear statement that no environment (including self-hosted) executed these.

Full unauthenticated request bodies logged at info level

The endpoint logs `logger.info("browser_report_received", extra={"request_body": request.data})` for every request. This is an unauthenticated, CORS-enabled public endpoint (permission_classes = ()) that accepts arbitrary JSON payloads from browsers, including report `body` contents, URLs, and user agents (potential PII). Logging the entire body at info level in production will also produce unbounded log volume for large or malicious payloads. The request body should be omitted or logged at debug with size limits.

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered when a search query is present

`sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns the unfiltered sorted list when `searchQuery` is empty, and only applies the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(...)` filter inside the search branch. So `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are still shown when the user has not typed anything, but disappear as soon as they type — inconsistent behavior. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied unconditionally, before the search-substring filter.

Refactor swaps useApiQuery options for useQuery defaults, enabling retries and refetch-on-focus

The previous implementation used `useApiQuery` with `{staleTime: 0, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, retry: false}`. The new `useQuery` call passes only `enabled`, `queryKey`, and `queryFn`, so react-query defaults now apply: up to 3 retries with exponential backoff on failure and refetch on window focus. Since this hook drives search-bar attribute-key suggestions (called per keystroke/interaction), failed requests will now be retried 3 times and refetch when the user refocuses the window, increasing load on the trace-items attributes endpoint and changing observed latency/error behavior. Preserve the original query options (retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false) or set them explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is a read-modify-write race (TOCTOU)

In the credentials authorize() handler, the backup code is validated with `backupCodes.indexOf(...)` and then consumed by re-encrypting and writing the whole array back via prisma.user.update. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both pass the indexOf check before either write lands, so a single-use code can be redeemed twice. The update should be conditional/atomic (or use a transaction/optimistic check) to guarantee one-time use, since 'each backup code can be used exactly once' is the stated security contract.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code is consumed before the login is guaranteed to succeed

The verified backup code is marked used (set to null and persisted) inside authorize(), before next-auth finishes signing the user in (JWT encoding, signIn callback, session creation). If any later step fails, the user has permanently lost a backup code without gaining access. The consumption should only happen once the sign-in is committed, or be idempotent/retryable.

Backup codes compared with indexOf (non-constant-time)

Backup codes are compared using `Array.prototype.indexOf`, which uses non-constant-time string comparison on a secret. For consistency with how passwords/TOTP are verified, a timing-safe comparison is preferable, though the practical exploitability is low given network jitter. Low priority hardening.

Empty backup code submission silently does nothing on login

The login form has `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the BackupCode TextField are never enforced, and there is no zod/react-hook-form validation for `backupCode`. If a user in the 'lost access' flow submits without typing a code, `credentials.backupCode` is empty/falsy, so the authorize() branch `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is skipped, the totpCode branch throws SecondFactorRequired, and the client just re-sets twoFactorRequired(true) — no error message is shown and nothing happens. The user gets no feedback.

No test actually exercises backup-code login or backup-code 2FA disable

The PR adds backup codes as the core feature but the e2e suite only tests downloading/copying/closing the backup-code dialog. There is no test that logs in with a backup code (the primary new auth path in next-auth-options.ts), verifies a code is single-use, or disables 2FA with a backup code (the new branch in disable.ts). These are security-critical code paths; a regression would go unnoticed.

req.body.backupCode is used without type/shape validation

The disable endpoint calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` without validating that it is a string. A client POSTing `backupCode` as an object/array/null-as-object (Next.js body parsing can produce nested JSON) causes `replaceAll is not a function`, throwing a 500. The login authorize() path in next-auth-options.ts (line 144) has the same unvalidated `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)`. Inputs should be validated (e.g. zod string) before use.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent/deleteEvent lose destination calendar fallback for legacy bookings

In updateEvent the new code is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is null/undefined (all bookings created before the externalCalendarId reference refactor, and any reference where it wasn't stored), the `.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against null/undefined and never matches, so selectedCalendar is undefined. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. The same broken pattern exists in deleteEvent (line 315-317). Result: updating or cancelling legacy Google bookings calls the API with calendarId undefined, which fails or hits the wrong calendar, so events on a non-primary destination calendar are never updated/deleted.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unrelated inversion of IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED slug condition

The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts when the org team gets a slug: previously the slug was set when team billing was NOT enabled and requestedSlug when it WAS; now slug is set when billing IS enabled. This is unrelated to the destinationCalendar work and silently changes organization subdomain creation behavior for self-hosted (non-billing) instances, which will now never get a slug set on team creation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Crash when destinationCalendar is empty/undefined and location is Google Meet

In EventManager.create, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` dereferences without optional chaining. When a booking has no destination calendars (evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array — which is now the normal case for users without a destination calendar, e.g. handleNewBooking sets null), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this line throws a TypeError, failing the whole booking creation whenever Google Meet is selected as location. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and was null-safe.

Error message in updateAllCalendarEvents catch no longer logged

The catch block previously did `console.error(message)`; the new code builds the same detailed message (including which credential/book failed) but never logs or reports it — it's only used in a template that is discarded. Failures inside updateAllCalendarEvents are now silent apart from the synthesized failure results, making production debugging of calendar update failures harder.

Lark/CalDav/Office365 services ignore per-destination calendars for multi-host events

LarkCalendarService.createEvent (and BaseCalendarService in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts line 156, and Office365CalendarService line 73) still only read the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`). EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates all destinations and calls createEvent per credential, but these services always create the event on the first host's calendar regardless of which destination/credential is being processed, so secondary hosts on Lark/CalDav/Office365 will either get duplicate events on the wrong calendar or no event on their own calendar — the exact bug this PR claims to fix, only fixed for Google Calendar.

Only the first destination calendar is persisted on the booking

When creating the booking, `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar && evt.destinationCalendar.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined` connects only the first destination calendar (the DB relation is single). For collective events, secondary hosts' destination calendars are only recoverable via the created bookingReferences; any code path that rebuilds a CalendarEvent from the booking (cancel, reschedule, requestReschedule, payment webhooks — all updated in this PR to `[booking.destinationCalendar]`) will only include the organizer's calendar. If reference creation fails or a reference lacks externalCalendarId, secondary hosts' calendar events become orphaned. Consider persisting all destinations or ensuring the fallback paths reconstruct the full list.

Organizer attendee email always set from first destination calendar, even when creating on another host's calendar

createEvent always uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` (the first entry of destinationCalendar) as the organizer attendee email. In the multi-host collective scenario this PR targets, the same event is created once per destination calendar with different credentials; for the second host's calendar the organizer email will still be the first host's externalId, producing a wrong organizer on that event and potentially bouncing attendee invites. The email should be derived from the destination matching the current credentialId (the `selectedCalendar`), not unconditionally from the first array entry.

Patch after insert uses possibly-undefined calendarId

In createEvent, the insert call falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent events.patch (used to add the hangout link to the description) passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. When no destinationCalendar matches the credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined and the patch request is sent with calendarId undefined, so the description/hangoutLink update silently fails (or errors) for every event created on the primary calendar.

credentialId dropped from video references in create()

In `referencesToCreate` inside create(), `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` discards the credentialId for video results. Previously it fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` for non-calendar results. While the old fallback was also wrong (it used the calendar's credential for video), the new code stores no credentialId at all for video references, which handleCancelBooking relies on (`bookingVideoReference.credentialId`) to find the video credential and delete the meeting on cancellation — cancelled bookings with video meetings will now leak the video meeting. createMeeting's EventResult should carry and propagate the video credential's id.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fake refresh_token literal "refresh_token" is persisted to credentials

When credential sync is enabled and the sync endpoint response lacks a refresh_token, the code assigns the literal string "refresh_token" to refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token. Callers (Office365, Zoom, etc.) then spread this into the credential key and write it to the DB via prisma.credential.update. The real refresh token is overwritten with a junk value, so if credential sync is later disabled (or the endpoint changes), the next token refresh will fail permanently and the integration breaks with an invalid_grant. The correct behavior is to preserve the previously stored refresh_token, not fabricate one.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Computed zod schema keys are "[object Object]" and effectively meaningless

The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the string "[object Object]", so the schema literally defines properties named "[object Object]" rather than "any numeric property is the expiry". In non-strict (strip) zod objects these keys are simply never matched, meaning: (1) no expiry field is validated at all, so callers like Google's refreshAccessToken read token.expiry_date as undefined and write undefined into the credential; (2) the comment's intent is not implemented. Token responses with missing/renamed expiry fields pass validation and corrupt stored credentials.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync branch returns a fetch Response, breaking axios-based callers that expect .data

When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a `fetch` Response object. But the zoho-bigin (CalendarService.ts line 85-96) and zohocrm (CalendarService.ts line 204-217) callers pass axios-based refresh functions and immediately access `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token`. A fetch Response has no `.data` property, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and these usages throw TypeError whenever credential sync is enabled — Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin refresh will crash instead of returning tokens. The abstraction leaks two incompatible response shapes.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync branch returns a fetch Response, breaking axios-based callers that expect .data

When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a `fetch` Response object. But the zoho-bigin (CalendarService.ts line 85-96) and zohocrm (CalendarService.ts line 204-217) callers pass axios-based refresh functions and immediately access `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token`. A fetch Response has no `.data` property, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and these usages throw TypeError whenever credential sync is enabled — Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin refresh will crash instead of returning tokens. The abstraction leaks two incompatible response shapes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
credentialId passed as userId to refreshOAuthTokens

In refreshAccessToken, the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens is `credentialId` (the credential's DB id) instead of `credential.userId`. When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint receives the credential id as `calcomUserId`, so the external app store looks up (or fails to look up) the wrong user entirely and returns tokens for the wrong account — or none.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
No HTTP method check and unhandled zod parse throws 500s

The handler never checks req.method, so GET/PUT etc. are processed; and `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on invalid payloads, which surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. Similarly JSON.parse of the decrypted payload (line 57) and symmetricDecrypt with an empty key (line 58, since CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY may be unset while APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is truthy only when both vars are set — but empty-string values in .env.example satisfy the check) can throw unhandled errors. Use safeParse, validate the method, and wrap decryption.

false_negatives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

false_positives.candidate:
APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed as the result of `process.env.X && process.env.Y`, i.e. `string | undefined`, not boolean. Truthiness works, but the .env.example ships `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=""` — an empty string, which is falsy, so copying the example file as-is silently disables the feature; conversely any non-empty value (e.g. "false") enables it. Export an explicit boolean (e.g. `!!(...)` or compare against "1"/"true") to avoid accidental misconfiguration.

Decrypted credential keys stored without any schema validation

The webhook decrypts the payload and stores `JSON.parse(...)` directly as the credential key with no validation against the app's expected key schema (e.g. googleCredentialSchema). A payload that is valid JSON but missing access_token/refresh_token/expiry, or containing arbitrary extra fields, is persisted verbatim to the user's credential. Since every calendar/video service parses this key with zod on next use, malformed keys break bookings for that user. Validate the decrypted keys against the app's credential schema before writing.

Google sync path writes undefined expiry_date into credential key

In the sync path, `res` is a fetch Response whose `.data` is undefined; `const token = res?.data` then makes `token.access_token` and `token.expiry_date` throw (reading property of undefined) or, if the endpoint returns the documented minimal shape without expiry_date, `googleCredentials.expiry_date` becomes undefined. parseRefreshTokenResponse with the relaxed minimum schema (which never validates expiry_date — see separate finding) then persists a credential with expiry_date: undefined. On the next getToken() call, `myGoogleAuth.isTokenExpiring()` will treat undefined expiry as expired, causing a refresh on every single API call and hammering the sync endpoint.

HubSpot sync response shape mismatch: fetch Response lacks expiresIn/accessToken

When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the code then reads `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` (lines 192, 202), which are undefined on a Response object. `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` yields NaN, and setAccessToken(undefined) is called — HubSpot requests will be made with an invalid Authorization header. The sync response needs to be `.json()`-ed and mapped to the HubspotToken shape (camelCase) before use.

Lark refresh relies on wrapped Response being consumed once

When sync is disabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the same fetch Response produced by the inner closure; that's fine. But when sync is enabled, the returned Response is from the sync endpoint and handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp> expects the Lark envelope `{code, data: {access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_expires_in}}`. A generic sync endpoint returning `{access_token, expires_in}` (as the PR description says: "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date") will fail handleLarkError's code check, and `data.data.refresh_token`/`refresh_expires_date` will be undefined — the stored Lark credential then has a garbage refresh_token and the next refresh deletes the credential. There is no contract alignment between the sync response format and each app's expected token shape.

Read-then-write credential creation is racy

The handler does findFirst then update/create without a transaction or unique constraint. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user+app can both see no existing credential and both create one, resulting in duplicate credentials for the same app/user (the code elsewhere, e.g. office365video/webex/zoom callbacks, has to work around exactly this duplicate-credential problem by deleting extras). Wrap in a transaction or use a unique constraint / upsert semantics.

Sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is unauthenticated and response unchecked

The POST to the credential sync endpoint sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header (no shared secret), so the receiving side cannot verify the request came from Cal.com — anyone who learns the endpoint URL can request token refreshes for arbitrary users. Additionally, `response.ok` is never checked; a 4xx/5xx (e.g. HTML error page) is returned to the caller and then parsed as a token response, producing confusing failures or corrupting credentials when combined with the relaxed minimumTokenResponseSchema.

prisma is used but never imported in SalesforceCalendarService

The new code in getClient() calls prisma.credential.update(...) (and the file's other new code references prisma), but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This is a compile/runtime error — the Salesforce calendar service will crash (ReferenceError) the first time a client is constructed, breaking all Salesforce integrations.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blacklist and duplicate email checks are case-sensitive

The blacklist is lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`), but `uniqueGuests` filters with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so any guest email with uppercase letters (e.g. "User@Spam.com") bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entirely. Similarly `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` is an exact-case compare, so the same attendee can be added twice under different casing, producing duplicate attendees and duplicate emails. Both comparisons should compare lowercased emails.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||, wrongly denying team admins

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, i.e. the caller must be BOTH an admin and an owner of the booking's team. A user who is a team admin but not the team owner (a common role) is denied with FORBIDDEN when adding guests to team bookings, even though the intent is clearly to allow either role. Should be `||`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event type metadata

Every other email-sending function in email-manager.ts (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, etc.) checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` so event types that disabled standard emails don't send them. The new `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no `eventTypeMetadata` and sends organizer and attendee emails unconditionally, breaking the 'disable standard emails' contract for this notification.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Calendar update uses the caller's credentials/user instead of the booking organizer's

`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` build the EventManager from the requesting user. When the requester is an attendee or a team admin (not the booking organizer), the calendar attendee update runs with the caller's calendar credentials, not the organizer's — the update to the organizer's calendar event will fail or, worse, act on the wrong account. The EventManager should be constructed from `booking.user` (which was already fetched with its credentials).

Email send errors swallowed without logging the error object

The catch block around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err`, so failures are undiagnosable in production. Additionally, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 is not wrapped in any error handling — if it throws, the attendees have already been persisted to the DB (line 92) and the mutation rejects while the guests are actually added, leaving DB and calendars out of sync with a confusing error shown to the user.

Guests stored with empty name and no validation of booking status

New guests are created with `name: ""`, so attendee lists and emails render blank names for these guests (e.g. `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${...}>`" produces `" <a@b.com>"`). Also, the handler does not check `booking.status`, so guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings, mutating data and sending 'guests added' emails for events that no longer exist.

No tests for the new addGuests endpoint

The PR adds a new mutation with non-trivial authorization rules (organizer / attendee / team admin), dedup and blacklist filtering, and email side effects, but no unit or e2e tests are added for any of this — particularly the currently-broken team-admin authorization (`&&` instead of `||`), which a test would have caught.

Stale validation error state when reopening the dialog

`isInvalidEmail` is only reset on the Cancel button click. If the user submits invalid emails (error shown), then closes the dialog via the X / overlay (Dialog onOpenChange) and reopens it, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error is still displayed even though the input was reset on success or still holds the old values otherwise. Validation state should reset when the dialog opens/closes or when the input changes.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

Both the failure path (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, computed from the value fetched at the start of the run. If two runs of this cron overlap (or a run is retried), increments are lost and a permanently failing reminder can be retried indefinitely, defeating the intended two-attempt limit. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.

Reminders skipped for missing message/sendTo never count a retry and never get cleaned up

Such a reminder stays `scheduled: false` and is re-fetched and re-skipped by every cron run until scheduledDate passes the 7-day window, wasting queries. Since this PR's stated goal is to stop endlessly reprocessing failing reminders, this skip path should also increment retryCount (or delete the reminder) so it is retired after two attempts.

If serialization sends the array as a JSON/text parameter rather than a Postgres array, `= ANY(...)` will throw a type error at query time — and since the PR author could not run the tests, this has not been verified. Caching tests removed without replacement

The previous test suite had a 'Caching' describe block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on second call. These tests were deleted entirely rather than converted to the new Prisma.sql format. The service still contains caching logic (`cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` with the undefined-vs-null distinction), and that logic is now completely untested; a regression in the caching (e.g. caching null filter conditions incorrectly) would go undetected.
